title: platform-standup-2026-03-10
content:
Platform Engineering — Standup notes
Date: 2026-03-10
Facilitator: Maya Patel
Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Rita, Samir, Lina, Alex (brief), Priya (remote)

Quick context: weekly sync covering control plane, routing, auth, quotas. Mostly operational updates, a couple of follow-ups on flaky quota enforcement and canary rollout behavior. Notes are intentionally terse — action items assigned at the bottom.

1) Control plane
- Progress: Canary rollout for the incremental rollback policy completed on 6% of traffic in us-west (deployment group A). No increased error rate observed in the last 24h. Observability dashboards (latency/p95 and error-rate) show stable trend.
- Work in flight: migrating DB session state to the new sharded-store (PLAT-482). Initial migration script executed in staging; found two query hotspots that need index hints. Samir to post optimized query and load test results by EOD 3/11.
- Blocker: automated canary promotion job intermittently times out when the control plane is under heavy GC. Root cause hypothesized to be a heap fragmentation issue in the rollout service JVM. Ethan to open a profiling run and attach heap dumps to JIRA-PLAT-501.
- Notes: we should add graceful backoff to the promotion job (retry window + exponential backoff). Agreed to include as a follow-up PR instead of hotfix to limit blast radius.

2) Routing
- Progress: Smart routing v2 landed on staging. This includes the policy engine change to route by latency-SLO with cost-weighted fallback. End-to-end tests passed but a couple of integration tests flaked (see github PR).
- Incident update: last Tuesday we saw increased 429s from the routing layer when a downstream dedicated pool reported transient OOMs. We mitigated by adding immediate fallback to hosted-compatible variants. Need a small improvement: prefer cross-region fallback only after local-other-pool fallback exhausted. Lina to update policy priority ordering (short patch, target 3/12).
- Perf note: routing decision CPU p50 is up ~8% under synthetic traffic with v2; will iterate on caching the policy eval. Action: Rita + Lina to prototype memoization for common route keys and measure impact.

3) Auth
- Progress: OAuth token refresh retry logic fix deployed to staging; fixed a race where concurrent refreshes invalidated a cache key and caused repeated failed auths. Observed successful flows in staging.
- Production bug: intermittent 401s reported on Dedicated customers using long-lived session tokens when a token-rotation hits during high concurrency. Hypothesis: the token rewriter sometimes emits a token with wrong aud claim if rotation window overlaps. Priya is drafting a repro harness.
- Action: add additional logging around token claims for rotation windows (Samir), and add a short-term mitigation to make rotation idempotent (deploy toggle behind feature flag). Target: mitigation by 3/13.

4) Quotas & Rate Limiting
- Ongoing: quota enforcement engine being updated to support burst windows per-customer (JIRA-PLAT-501). New algorithm (leaky bucket variant + dynamic refill) reduces false positives on short spikes but a regression in per-request latency was observed in staging.
- Debug: profiling indicates the bottleneck is centralized quota lookup RPC hitting the meta-cache more frequently than expected. Plan: add local LRU cache with TTL per routing instance to reduce RPCs. Estimated ~18% decrease in lookup rate in perf tests. Lina to prototype; ETA 3/12.
- Customer impact: two customers reported unexpected throttles during training jobs. Reproduced locally using synthetic load — tweak to burst window should alleviate. Reach out to CS to coordinate a patch window.

5) Observability & Alerting
- Added a new composite alert to detect canary promotion timeouts (control-plane.promote_timeout > 3m for 5m). First firing on 3/09 in staging — helped catch the JVM GC issue.
- Action: add playbook link to alert (Confluence page). Maya to update alert runbook with next steps and on-call contact.

6) Security & Compliance notes
- Private deployments: working through KMS integration test failures for on-prem package. Those are tracked in separate doc; no production impact.

7) Cross-team / Support notes
- CS flagged two Dedicated customers affected by quota regression. Decision: patch quota window in non-peak hours and notify customers. Samir to coordinate with Andrew (CS) for scheduling and rollback plan.
- Solutions Eng note: want a lightweight runbook for customers to understand fallback behavior when routing triggers model variant fallback. Lina to draft and share by 3/15.

8) Action items (owner — due)
- Samir: post optimized DB queries for sharded-store migration + load test results — due 2026-03-11 (JIRA-PLAT-482).
- Ethan: run profiler on rollout service, attach heap dumps to JIRA-PLAT-501 — due 2026-03-11.
- Lina: update routing policy priority ordering to prefer local-other-pool before cross-region fallback — due 2026-03-12.
- Rita + Lina: prototype memoization for policy eval caching and share perf numbers — due 2026-03-17.
- Samir: add rotation-window token claim logging and short-term idempotent rotation mitigation (feature-flagged) — due 2026-03-13.
- Lina: prototype local LRU cache for quota lookup, run perf tests — due 2026-03-12 (JIRA-PLAT-501).
- Maya: update canary promotion alert runbook with playbook link and on-call contact — due 2026-03-11.
- Samir: coordinate patch window with Andrew (CS) for quota regression customers — due 2026-03-12.

Decisions made:
- Do not hotfix the canary promotion job; instead add backoff and address JVM GC root cause in next sprint.
- Prefer small, feature-flagged mitigations for auth rotation (to reduce blast radius) before larger refactor.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we move canary promotion job to a separate smaller JVM process to avoid GC coupling? (Maya to discuss with infra on 3/11)
- Is the memoization approach for routing policy eval safe for multi-tenant keys? Need security review — Lina to create a short ADR and loop in security.

Notes to self / informal:
- Saw a spike in debug logs from rota-service around 03:20 UTC — likely noise from load test; keep an eye.
- Remember to follow up with legal on customer data handling notes for Private KMS tests.

Next standup: 2026-03-17 (same time).

-- end of standup notes --
